subject: Request: exportable admin event digest and SLA/retention clarification for SOC 2
messages:
From: Samantha Gray <s.gray@novamed.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: exportable admin event digest and SLA/retention clarification for SOC 2

Hi Tessa / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SOC 2 evidence collection for NovaMed we need a clear description and a sample export of Redwood's admin/activity telemetry. Specifically can you confirm: 

- Which admin event types are captured (sign-ins, role changes, API key rotations, model/promote/deploy actions, policy changes, console actions, dedicated-node actions, etc.)
- Default retention for audit-grade admin events and options to extend (and cost model if any)
- Export formats you can provide (JSONL, CSV manifest, signed tarball, streaming feed) and a recommended format for a typical auditor package
- Redaction/PII-handling options and whether we can request field-level redaction at snapshot time
- Delivery methods you support (SFTP with client cert, pre-signed cloud storage link, signed Drive folder) and whether you can provide checksums/HMAC-attested manifests

We are aiming to bundle a 30-day sample plus a point-in-time snapshot for the audit team. Can you share a sample manifest and a short playbook describing the handoff steps and timelines?

Appreciate a reply by end of week so our audit timeline can be confirmed.

Best,
Samantha
Senior IT Risk Analyst
NovaMed

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Gray <s.gray@novamed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: exportable admin event digest and SLA/retention clarification for SOC 2

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise scoping answer plus what we can deliver as a sample bundle. I'll follow up with the export playbook attached.

What Redwood logs (high-level):
- Authentication: interactive console logins, API token usage, OAuth grants, MFA events (success/failure).
- Access & identity changes: role assignments, group changes, SSO config updates, service account creation/deletion.
- Secrets & keys: API key creation/rotation/deletion events (no secret values in logs).
- Model & serving lifecycle: model uploads, version pins, rollouts/canary promotions, config changes (batch sizes, quantization toggles).
- Policy/ACL changes: RBAC updates, route-level policy edits, ACL grants/revokes.
- Infrastructure ops (admin): dedicated capacity allocations, node reboots, scaling events, maintenance windows.
- Tenant actions: data export requests, retention configuration changes, consent/opt-out events.

Retention & retention options:
- Default: 365 days for audit-level admin/identity events.
- Options: 1) Extended retention add-on (2–7 years) 2) Shorter rolling windows (90/180/365) selectable per-account.
- Exportable archives: cold snapshots (compressed, signed) retained for configurable windows; we can produce on-demand historical slices beyond default retention if arranged in advance.

Export formats & recommendations:
- Raw: gzipped JSONL (each event as a single JSON line) — best for ingestion.
- Manifest: CSV manifest with per-file checksums, record counts, time-range, timezone normalization notes. We include a manifest schema sample.
- Attestation: tar.gz bundle + signed SHA256 checksum file; optional HMAC attestation using a customer-shared key.
- For auditors: recommended deliverable = (1) day-of snapshot (gz JSONL) + (2) 30-day sample binned by day + (3) CSV manifest + (4) attested checksum.

Redaction & PII handling:
- We never record raw secrets/credentials.
- PII fields (user email, IP) can be hashed or redacted at export time. Two modes: pseudonymize (deterministic hash) or redact (remove values).
- Field-level redaction requires advance request and a short blackout to produce the attested snapshot (we note redaction in the manifest).

Delivery & custody:
- Supported: SFTP (mutual-TLS + client cert), pre-signed S3 GCS links (timeboxed), shared Drive folder (signed link) with attestation, or secure transfer to your SFTP endpoint.
- We provide signed manifests (SHA256) and can HMAC the manifest with a customer-provided key for added proof.

Sampling & snapshots:
- We provide: daily binned exports, contiguous N-day slices, and point-in-time snapshots.
- SOC 2 guidance we follow: include both a contiguous sample window (30 days) and at least one full-day signed snapshot to demonstrate timeline integrity.

Deliverables we can provide as a sample bundle (what we propose to send quickly):
- admin_activity_sample_manifest.csv (CSV manifest example, includes checksum column)
- one-day gzipped JSONL snapshot (sample day) — small subset clipped for security
- export_playbook_v2.pdf (playbook describing handoff steps and custody)
- query_snippet.sql (the extraction filter used to create the sample)

Timeline & next steps:
- Sample bundle: within 3 business days if we have your target date range.
- Production/attested export: typical lead time 7–14 business days (includes HMAC setup, redaction run, and QA).

I've attached the playbook; the sample manifest and query snippet will follow in the sample bundle. If you want mutual-TLS SFTP we'll need a host + cert details before the snapshot run.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0192

Attachment: export_playbook_v2.pdf (playbook stub, 28 pages)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Gray <s.gray@novamed.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: exportable admin event digest and SLA/retention clarification for SOC 2

Samantha / Tessa — quick clarifications from the infra side: 

- Credential events: logs will show creation/rotation/deletion metadata, not secret values. We also surface the actor and the initiating IP (IP can be redacted or pseudonymized per request).
- Live streaming vs snapshot: we support a near-real-time audit stream (pub/sub) for customers with streaming ingestion needs, but for SOC 2 most auditors prefer sealed snapshots plus manifests.
- On-demand slices: if you need a noncontiguous slice (e.g., all 'role change' events across 1 year) we can generate that, but it requires a query job and additional validation time.
- Retention-change audit: we record and export retention configuration changes themselves as admin events (useful to show no back-dating or retention tampering).

If the auditor wants an HMAC key exchange we should coordinate an OTP for key handshake — recommend we schedule that step before snapshot.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly what we need. We confirm we want:

- 30-day contiguous sample (June 1–30, 2026) binned by day

- Pseudonymize IP addresses (deterministic hash)
- Delivery to our SFTP endpoint (sftp.novamed.com) — we'll send cert details in a separate secure message

Please proceed with the sample bundle. Timeline: sample within 3 business days would be perfect for our audit prep.

Also please include the CSV manifest and the query snippet in the bundle. 

Samantha
